newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Chrysler dividend pumps volume.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Chrysler dividend pumps volume.

text.p: Chrysler Corp goes ex-dividend Wednesday, which led to a surge in options trading on three January calls.
The Chrysler January 25 traded 27,615 contracts, the January 27-1/2 call traded about 17,240 and the January 20 traded more than 14,000. The January 22-1/2 call traded 6,300 contracts.
"It's all dividend plays," a trader at the Chicago Board Options Exchange said of the Chrysler volume.
Chrysler shares fell 3/8 to 35-3/4 on consolidated volume of about 2.31 million shares.

"Tonight, all the long options will be exercised by the individuals anticipating that statistically they will all not be assigned against their short positions and therefore they will have some unoptioned stock to sell out when Chrysler trades ex-dividend tomorrow," explained Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co.
Chrysler goes ex-dividend Tuesday for a dividend payable on January 15. The quarterly dividend is $0.40.
Schwartz said historically, stocks do not lose their full dividend amount.
"So people are speculating they will capture some portion of that 40-cent dividend after they sell the stock out tomorrow ex-dividend," he said.

Options volume in Chrysler is likely to slow to normal levels Wednesday, but it could continue to be pumped up a bit as some investors unwind options positions that were not exercised, Schwartz added.
